 JUDGMENT

This case emerges from the charge sheet filed by the PSI of Yalahanka Upanagara police station in Crime No.92/2015 against the accused No. 1 to 3 for the offences punishable U/Sec. 63 & 68(A) of Copy Right Act and Sec.420 of IPC.
C.C.No.6564/2018 02.

The brief case of the prosecution is as under:-
The accused No.1 is having the xerox shop by name 'Verma enterprises' and accused No.2 is having xerox shop by name 'SRSA Stationary' in room No.713 & 712 respectively near Sheshadripuram College, A Sector, Yelahanka Upanagara of Yelahanka Upanagara Police Station limits.

The CW.1 on receiving the credible information furnished by Neeraj books has conducted the raid on 24.04.2015 at about 1 PM in the presence of CW.2 and the mahazar witnesses CW.3 & 4 with the aid CW.5 & 6 to 'Verma Enterprises' and to 'SRSA Stationary' and found that, the accused persons by using xerox machine were scanning the books published by Neeraj books for BBM and B.Com., and selling the xerox copies of the books by infringing the copy right over the said books of Neeraj company and the accused No.3 being the owner of said shops has co-operated accused No.1 & 2 and due to such acts of the accused, the Neeraj books having copy right over the books published by them have suffered loss and the accused cheated the public by making unlawful gain and thus the accused have committed the offence.

03 . On the basis of raid conducted by CW.1 seizure of the books and the xerox copies of the same from the accused, he has lodged C.C.No.6564/2018 the complaint with CW.7 and on the basis of such report of CW.1, CW.7 has registered the case in Crime No.92/2015 and dispatched the FIR to this court and thereafter he has investigated the matter and CW.1 has further investigated the matter and after completion of investigation, he has filed the charge sheet against accused No.1 to 3 for the above said offences.

sentences.text: On the basis of charge sheet, this court has taken cognizance of the offence and secured the presence of accused No.1 to 3 and they are released on bail.

The charge sheet copy and other prosecution papers were furnished to the accused by complying the provisions of Section 207 of Cr.P.C.
05.
After hearing learned APP and learned counsel for the accused, charges were framed against the accused persons for the offences punishable U/Sec. 63 & 68(A) of Copy Right Act and Sec.420 of IPC.
The accused have denied the charges as false and pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
06. The prosecution, in order to prove its case, has examined 3 witnesses as PW.1 to PW.3 and got marked as 2 documents as Ex.P.1 & Ex.P.2 and got identified the seized books as MO.1.
The prosecution has not secured the presence of CW.2, 3, 4 & 7 inspite C.C.No.6564/2018 of issuance of repeated process such as summons, warrant and proclamation.
Therefore, vide order dated 01.03.2024 the evidence of CW.2, 3, 4 & 7 is dropped.

After closure of evidence of the prosecution,
the incriminating circumstances in the evidence of the prosecution is recorded and read over to the accused and their statement under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. recorded.
The accused no.1 to 3 have denied the incriminating circumstances as false and not chosen to lead their evidence.
07. Heard arguments of learned Sr.APP and learned counsel for accused.
Perused the records.

08. Following points arise for the consideration of this court:-
POINTS 01.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, on 24.04.2015 at 1 pm, the accused No.1 in shop No.713 bearing name and style 'Verma Enterprises'
and accused No.2 in a shop No.712 under the name and style to 'SRSA stationary'
near Sheshadripuram College, A Sector, Yelahanka Upanagara have found selling the xerox copies by prepared through the xerox machine by scanning the BBM and B.Com., books published by Neeraj Books company which is having copy C.C.No.6564/2018 right over the same and selling the same to the public by causing loss to the Neeraj companies and to the public and making unlawful gain for himself and thus he has violated the copy right of Neeraj books and thus committed the offence punishable under section 63 & 68(A) Copy Right Act and under section 420 of IPC ?
02. What order or sentence?
09.

The findings of this court to the above points is as under:-
Points No.1 : In the Negative, Point No.2 : As per the final order, for the following:-

sentences.text: 10 . Points No.1:-
To prove the case, the prosecution has been examined CW.1 as PW.1.
He is the police official who conducted the raid and lodged the complaint.

In his evidence he has deposed that, on 24.04.2015 at 11 AM the authorized officer of Neeraj Book company has given written information to them about violation of copy right and making copies of the books with the xerox machine and on such information, he has conducted the raid to 'Verma Enterprises' at 13th A Main Road of Yelahanka at 12.30 pm.,

He has deposed that, at that time the accused No.1 Manjunath was present C.C.No.6564/2018 in the spot and by informing the purpose of the raid and he has verified the shop and found that, accused no. 1 was violating the copy right and found the products and seized the same and taken custody of accused no.1.

He has deposed that based on the information given by accused no.1, he has conducted the raid to 'SRSA Stationary' and the accused No.2 Yashavanth Kumar was present and on verification, they have found infringement of copy right and seized the materials.
He has deposed that, he has drawn the mahazar in the spot as per Ex.P.1 and lodged the complaint with CW.7 as per Ex.P.2.
He has has identified 10 books seized by him as MO.1.
Thus, the PW.1 has deposed about the raid conducted by him on the basis of the information given by representatives of Neeraj books.
In the cross examination he has deposed that, he has not investigated the matter.
He has only conducted the raid and lodged the complaint.
In his cross examination he has deposed that, the accused were found scanning the original text books of Neeraj Books company and taking the xerox copy of the same and selling the same to the public.
In the cross examination, he has denied all the suggestions of Learned Counsel for the accused.
The prosecution has examined CW. 6 as PW.2 & CW. 5 as PW.3.
They are the police officials who assisted PW.1 at the time of raid.
The PW.2 & 3 in their chief examination have deposed in concurrence to the case of the prosecution and the evidence of PW.1.
The PW.1 to 3 in their evidence have not deposed anything about the role of the accused No.3 in the alleged offence.
As per the case of the prosecution, the accused no.3 is the owner of the premises and accused No.1 & 2 were running the shop in the said building.
But, the PW.1 to 3 have not deposed anything about the involvement of accused no.3 in the alleged act of accused No.1 & 2 in their xerox shops.
In their cross examination, they have denied all the suggestions of Learned Counsel for the accused.
They have deposed that, they have not sealed the books or the xerox papers seized from the spot at the time of seizure.
In the cross examination PW 2 and 3 were not able to identify the accused persons individually with their names.
12. As per the case of the prosecution, CW.3 & 4 are the witnesses to the raid and mahazar drawn by PW.1.
But the prosecution has not examined the independent mahazar witnesses CW.3 & 4.
As per the case of the prosecution, CW.2 is the Assistant manager of Neeraj C.C.No.6564/2018 books, who lodged the information to CW.1 about obtaining xerox of the original books published by them.
He is also not appeared before this court inspite of issuance of repeated process and prosecution has not examined CW.2.
As per the case of the prosecution, CW.7 is the Investigating Officer who registered the case, lodged the FIR and investigated the matter.
But the prosecution has not examined CW.7 before this court.

Therefore, there is no material evidence on record to prove the line of investigation conducted by CW.7 and how he has came to the conclusion that there is sufficient material evidence is collected against the accused No.1 to 3 to prove the guilt.

Therefore, non-examination of CW.2 Yeshwanth Kumar Pi vs Manjunath Thippanna Kumbara on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78895979/

13. In the absence of evidence of the Investigating Officer and independent mahazar witnesses to the seizure mahazar, only on the evidence of the police officials who conducted the raid PW.1 to 3, it cannot concluded that the prosecution has proved the guilt.
The evidence of PW.1 to 3 requires corroboration from the independent witness.

Therefore, no credit can be attached to the evidence of PW.1 C.C.No.6564/2018 to 3 without any corroboration to find the guilt of the accused No.1 to 3.
14.

During the course of arguments, Learned Counsel for the accused has much argued that, making of the xerox of the text books for the purpose of education will not amount to an act of infringement of copy right.

As discussed above, there is no material on record to prove that MO.1 xerox copies of the BBM and B.Com. text books published by Neeraj books is seized from the custody of accused No.1 to 3 and they were copying the books and making the xerox and selling to the public or to the students.
In the decision relied by the accused between The Chancellor Masters and Scholars of University Oxford Vs. Rameshwari
Photo copy
If reproduction includes the plural, it cannot be held that, making of multiple copies would be impermissible.
It happens in law that, foot prints of one concept fall on the territory of other, but that does not mean that, the farmer should be restricted."

Thus, by observing so the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has held that;
"Photocopied materials is made available to the students for meaningful discussions for the purpose of education will not amount to publication of the copy.".
Thus, by relying this decision, the Learned Counsel for the accused has argued that, the reproduction of the material for the purpose of education will not amount to infringement of copy right.
The Hon'ble High Court has held by applying the provisions of section 52 (i) of Copy Right act has held
that the production of work by a teacher or a people in the course of instructions are as a part of questions to be answered in the examination will not amount to an infringement of copy right
. Admittedly, the shops of the accused persons is doing the business of xerox and it is situated near Sheshadripuram College.
It is not the case of the prosecution that, the accused persons were preparing the books by obtaining the xerox copies of the papers and publishing the same in their own name.
It is C.C.No.6564/2018 also not the case of the prosecution that, the accused are collecting more money than the xerox charges while selling the said xerox copies.

sentences.text: Therefore, upon considering this aspects it is clear that, mere reproduction of the copies of the books for the purpose of education of the children will not amount to an act of infringement of copy right.
Further more, there is no conclusive material has been placed by the prosecution to prove the raid conducted by PW.1 to 3.
The independent witnesses are not examined, the Investigating Officer is not examined and the prosecution has not proved the seizure of the articles from the custody of accused.
Therefore, even on merits based on evidence, the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused charged against them.
Therefore, the benefit of doubt in the case of the prosecution have to be extended to the accused.
Therefore, by extending the benefit of doubt in the case of the prosecution to the accused, this court answers the above Points No.1 in the Negative.
15. Point No.2:-

In view of the findings recorded to the above points, this court proceed to pass the following:-
C.C.No.6564/2018 ORDER

By exercising powers conferred U/sec. 248(1) of Cr.P.C.,
the accused No.1 to 3 are acquitted of the offences punishable U/Sec. 63 & 68(A) of Copy Right Act and Sec.420 of IPC.

The bail bond and surety bond of the accused No.1 to 3 shall continue in force for a period of 6 months for the purposes of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C.
The accused No.1 to 3 are set at liberty.
The property marked as MO.1 being the xerox copies of the books are worthless and ordered to be destroyed as worthless after appeal period is over.
(Dictated to the stenographer, transcribed by her, corrected directly on computer and then pronounced by me in open court on this the day of 12th day of July 2024).
(Sri Gokula K.) IX Addl.Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru City.
